title: A nontrivial universal homeomorphism of spectra yields either square and cube relations or a prime and a p-th power relation

standard_prerequisites.name: A ring extension inducing a universal homeomorphism on spectra is integral, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives integrality, which drives the reduction to a single generator and finiteness.

standard_prerequisites.name: Passing to a subalgebra generated by one element when testing the conclusion, and the closedness and nonemptiness of the support of a nonzero finite module, cited from the same chapter and the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces to a finite extension and produces a nonempty closed support whose minimal prime can be localized at.

standard_prerequisites.name: The conclusion is preserved by localizing the extension at a prime, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the reduction to a local base with the support of the quotient equal to the maximal ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: Two consecutive powers of an element lying in the base imply the square and cube alternative, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Delivers the first alternative of the conclusion when the prime of the extension is not contained in the base.

standard_prerequisites.name: A universally injective ring map with a nontrivial purely inseparable residue field extension has prime characteristic p with the extension purely inseparable, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the prime p and the element b of the second alternative in the remaining case.

core_obligations: Repeat the reduction of the preceding argument in full: use integrality to assume the extension is generated by one element and hence finite, take a minimal prime of the support of the quotient and localize there, so that the base is local with maximal ideal m, the extension is finite and the support of the quotient is exactly m (proof lines 11671-11683).

Split into the two alternatives: with I the annihilator of the quotient one has m equal to the radical of I, and the unique prime of the extension over m is the radical of IB, so every element of that prime has two consecutive powers in the base and the first alternative follows when it is not contained in the base; if it is contained in the base then the two residue fields are not isomorphic, and the cited result on universally injective maps makes the residue field extension purely inseparable of prime characteristic p, so an element of the larger residue field outside the smaller one whose p-th power lies in the smaller one gives an element b outside the base with pb and b to the p in the base (proof lines 11684-11709).
proof_roadmap: Write out the same reduction as for the residue field case (integral, one generator, finite, localize at a minimal prime of the support), then split according to whether the prime of the extension lies over the base, obtaining either the square and cube alternative or a purely inseparable residue field extension in prime characteristic and hence the p-th power alternative (proof lines 11671-11709).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a nontrivial ring extension whose spectrum map is a universal homeomorphism contains either an element outside the base with square and cube in the base, or an element outside the base with a prime multiple and a p-th power in the base (statement lines 11656-11663). The counted proof, 45 lines, is written out in full by the author even though it parallels an earlier argument: it reduces to an integral extension generated by one element and then finite, localizes at a minimal prime of the support of the quotient, identifies the unique prime of the extension over the maximal ideal of the base through the annihilator of the quotient, and then splits into the two alternatives, the second of which uses pure inseparability of the residue field extension in prime characteristic to build the required element (proof lines 11665-11709). It is H2 under the lane rule: the proof contains checkable reductions and a construction of the witnessed element in each alternative, and the opening sentence in which the author says the argument is almost the same as an earlier one is immediately followed by the full argument, so nothing is deferred.
